THE UNDERLINE REACHES 10-MILE MILESTONE
MIAMI-DADE CELEBRATES NEW 10-MILE UNDERLINE BIKE AND WALK PATH

A significant milestone has arrived for our area as residents and leaders come together to celebrate the completion of The Underline.

Present and past elected officials representing Miami-Dade County, the City of Miami, the City of Coral Gables, and the City of South Miami joined local residents for a formal ribbon cutting ceremony.

Attendees gathered to commemorate the latest achievement for the project: the finished 10-mile bike-and-walk path that runs through the participating communities. The completed route marks a major celebration for walkers, runners, and cyclists across the county.

items.desc: The proposal doesn’t name the coming state ban on government-funded DEI initiatives. Instead, it cites ‘changes in applicable law.’

headlines: MIAMI-DADE COMMISSIONERS TO VOTE ON ECONOMIC ADVOCACY TRUST REWRITE
MAJOR CHANGES PLANNED FOR HISTORIC MIAMI-DADE ECONOMIC TRUST
BORN AFTER 1980 RIOTS, MIAMI-DADE TRUST FACES BIG SHIFT
draft.article: Miami-Dade County Commissioners will take a final vote Tuesday, Nov. 17, on an ordinance reshaping the Miami-Dade Economic Advocacy Trust. Sponsored by Commissioner Oliver Gilbert, the measure directs the agency to shift its focus from Black residents to lower-income and economically distressed individuals across the county. The change comes weeks before state law SB 1134, signed by Governor Ron DeSantis to restrict government DEI efforts, takes effect. The Trust originated in 1983 following the Miami riots sparked by the death of Arthur McDuffie. Under Gilbert's proposal, the agency will keep running Teen Court and housing assistance for buyers earning up to 140 percent of the area median income, while ending trustee demographic mandates.

headlines: MIAMI DADE TAX COLLECTOR BACKS STATE PROBE INTO DSA
DARIEL FERNANDEZ SUPPORTS INQUIRY INTO DSA FOREIGN CONTRIBUTIONS
MIAMI OFFICIAL DEMANDS ANSWERS ON ALLEGED FOREIGN POLITICAL TIES
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez has voiced full support for Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier's investigation into the Democratic Socialists of America. The state probe centers on potential foreign contributions and financial links involving communist China and the Cuban dictatorship.

Fernandez, speaking as a Cuban American, emphasized his firsthand understanding of the harm caused by Cuba's regime. He stated that political ideology must not exempt organizations from the law and stressed the need to safeguard American institutions against unlawful foreign influence.

Demanding transparency for the public, Fernandez stated that any potential financial ties require strict scrutiny and that proven violations must bring consequences.

headlines: MAN ARRESTED FOR MURDER AFTER WOMAN FOUND AT GIBSON PARK
GIBSON PARK STRANGULATION LEADS TO MURDER CHARGE
MIAMI POLICE ARREST SUSPECT OUTSIDE CAMILLUS HOUSE AFTER HOMICIDE
draft.article:
Miami Police have arrested 45-year-old Jarmane Bradwell on a second-degree murder charge after a woman was found dead at Gibson Park. First responders arrived at the park around 6:45 p.m. on Nov. 4, where the victim was pronounced deceased at the scene. The county medical examiner later ruled her death a homicide caused by strangulation.

A witness reported hearing the couple arguing on park bleachers, during which the victim cried out that she was being choked. According to police, Bradwell told the witness he believed he killed his girlfriend and planned to take a bus to Georgia.

Officers intercepted Bradwell on Wednesday in a rideshare outside Camillus House at 1603 Northwest Seventh Avenue. He denied harming her, claiming he returned from buying drugs to find her dead. Bradwell is held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center.

headlines: PLAYBOY BUYS FREEHAND HOTEL IN MIAMI BEACH FOR $12.5M
PLAYBOY BRINGS PRIVATE CLUB TO MIAMI BEACH
HISTORIC FREEHAND HOTEL BECOMING PLAYBOY MEMBERS ONLY CLUB
draft.article:
Playboy is expanding its South Beach presence with a $12.5 million deal to purchase the Freehand Hotel at 27th Street and Indian Creek Drive. The purchase of the five-building, 89-room property from London-based Generator is scheduled to close on December 15.

The brand plans to convert the historic 1936 site, home to the popular Broken Shaker bar, into a private, members-only club. Playboy put down approximately $5 million for the acquisition, aiming to recoup costs through club memberships.

The move marks a return to the local hospitality scene after decades away. Playboy also announced plans to relocate its headquarters from Los Angeles to a penthouse at 1691 Michigan Avenue.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS OFFICIALLY CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4 1836
MIAMI AREA ROOTS TRACED BACK TO 1836
HOW OUR REGION BECAME DADE COUNTY IN 1836
draft.article:
Dade County officially came into existence on February 4, 1836. The newly established county received its official name in honor of Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River.

The year 1836 marked a defining chapter for the development of our area. In that exact same year, Fort Dallas was built right here along the frontier landscape.

The newly constructed Fort Dallas immediately served as an active military installation during the Second Seminole War. Together, the strategic military outpost and the formal designation of the county set the original groundwork for the historic footprint of our Miami community.
